Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations
Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.) To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation. If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.
Viewing City Council Meetings
Members of the public may view the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.azusaca.gov/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website. Your attendance at this public meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice as previously described.
Procedures for Addressing the Council
The Council encourages interested people to address this legislative body by making public comments. Public comments may be made during designated agendized public comment periods and during public hearing items. Public comments are limited to five (5) minutes per speaker, unless a different time is announced by the Mayor/presiding Chair.
The Council encourages free expression of all points of view. To allow all persons the opportunity to speak, please keep your remarks brief. If others have already expressed your position, you may simply indicate that you agree with a previous speaker. If appropriate, a spokesperson may present the views of your entire group. State law generally prohibits the City Council from responding to or acting upon matters not listed on this agenda. Council rules prohibit clapping, booing, or shouts of approval or disagreement from the audience. Clapping, booing, shouting or other actions from the audience which, disturbs, impedes, or otherwise renders infeasible the meeting’s orderly conduct, who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers or remote participation platform.

Works Superintendent – Parks Facilities Chavez, Director of Community Resources Carpenter, Management
Analyst - CMO Nazarian, City Clerk Services Manager Juarez.

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Kim Antol.

The Invocation was led by Venerable Nicholas Thanissaro.

CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Richman reported that Closed Session consisted of three items, and there was no reportable
action taken.

PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

Phra Nicholas Thanissaro, Buddhist Meditation Center invited the community to the Full Moon Meditation on
December 4, 2025.

Sal Covarrubias, Urban Forester for North Star Landcare, provided information about the company and his role
should the Council decide to award the tree maintenance contract to his company.

Ernesto Macias, Tree Service Kings representative, expressed concerns regarding Item D-3 related to the
qualifications of West Coast Arborists and North Star Landcare to complete line clearance work; and expressed
concern regarding the base bid amounts shown in Attachment 1.

Patrick Mahoney, Owner of West Coast Arborist, requested that the company be awarded the tree maintenance
contract; and stated the many ways in which the company supports the City.

John Pineda, West Coast Arborist representative, provided information on his background and qualifications;
stated the ways in which the company has supported the community; and requested that the Council consider
awarding the contract to the company.

Manuel Briano, West Coast Arborist tree trimmer, stated that he is a resident of Azusa; provided background on
his experience providing service to the City; and thanked the Council for considering the company for the
contract.

Tony Martinez, owner of North Star Landcare, provided background on his experience; described the
qualifications of the company; stated ways in which the company could provide improvements to the City; and
requested that the Council award the tree maintenance contract to the company.

City Clerk Cornejo stated that written communication was submitted by Gerard Batista.

REPORTS, UPDATES, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

City Manager Communications

City Manager Gonzalez introduced new City Attorney, Rachel Richman; announced the following events: the
grand opening of Vallarta Supermarket, the Canyon City Dog Park ribbon cutting on December 13, and a
reception in honor of outgoing Mayor Gonzales on December 15.

City Council Minutes  Page | 2
December 1, 2025
 Councilmember Announcements

Mayor Pro Tem Alvarez announced the following events: the Art of Gift Wrapping and Art classes in Spanish
“Hecho A Mano” at the Azusa Library; and asked the community to keep the two National Guardsmen who
were shot in Washington, D.C., in their prayers.

Councilmember Avila announced the following events: Festival of Lights and tree lighting - December 6, and
Encouragement Community Church – A Christmas Musical Spectacular on December 12.

Councilmember Mendez announced the following events: Azusa Craft Night – December 8, yard sales –
December 6 and 7; requested that a certificate be presented to the outgoing President of the Citrus Valley
Association of Realtors; congratulated Azusa High School for being featured on channel 2; and announced the
Santa Tour on December 21.

Councilmember Bow announced the following events: free after school tutoring for AUSD students at the
Azusa Library, the Azusa City Library groundbreaking ceremony on December 10, and Holiday Melodies on
December 17; and reminded the community about “Giving Tuesday” as an opportunity to give back to the
community.

Mayor Gonzales announced the following events: Holiday Night Market – December 11; encouraged the
community to check on the senior population during the holiday season; and expressed his gratitude toward his
colleagues in honor of the holiday season.

SCHEDULED ITEMS

CONSIDERATION TO ADOPT A RESOLUTION TO ALLOW FOR LIMITED STREET CLOSURES FOR
THE AZUSA NIGHT MARKET TAKING PLACE ON THURSDAY, DECEMBER 11, 2025

Management Analyst - CMO Nazarian requested the adoption of a resolution authorizing the temporary street
closures necessary for the Azusa Night Market which is scheduled to be held on December 11 from 5:00 p.m. to
9:00 p.m., with the required street closures extending from 6th Street to Foothill Boulevard.

Council subsequently commented on the hard work staff put into planning the event and expressed appreciation
to the Public Works Department for their assistance with the holiday lighting.

Moved by Councilmember Mendez, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Alvarez and carried by unanimous vote of the
Council to authorize and adopt Resolution No. 2025-C54 to allow for the temporary street closure and use of
the public right-of way on North Azusa Ave between 6th St. And Foothill Blvd. for the Azusa Night Market.

CONSIDERATION TO AWARD A THREE-YEAR CITYWIDE TREE MAINTENANCE CONTRACT FOR
PARK, PARKWAYS, MEDIAN ISLANDS AND UTILITY RIGHT OF WAY TREES IN RESPONSE TO
THE CITY’S REQUEST FOR QUALIFICATIONS

Mayor Gonzales recused himself from Item D-3 due to a potential perception of conflict of interest regarding
familial connection.

Director of Public Works and City Engineer Delgadillo stated that at the November 17 Council Meeting, the
Council requested that this item be brought back for consideration at this meeting; noted that correspondence
received since the last meeting was attached to the staff report; and advised the Council that Staff and
representatives were available to answer questions.

The Council requested clarification regarding the qualifications of applicants for the Tree Maintenance contract,
and the correspondence received referencing a “formal protest” related to the submitted proposals, and the
City’s qualifications and guidelines for clearing active utility lines.

In response to questions, Staff responded that five of the six applicants were deemed qualified; clarified that the
terminology “formal protest” was not applicable, as this item was not a Notice Inviting Bids; and further
explained that the City’s qualifications require experience and supervision by a certified utility line clearing
supervisor.

Further discussion took place regarding the importance of having a contract in place and the option of offering a
one-year contract to a vendor. The Council proposed offering North Star Landcare a one-year contract.

Moved by Councilmember Bow, seconded by Councilmember Avila to award North Star Landcare a one-year
contract for tree maintenance services.
